hypothesis: I will reproduce the FM baseline exactly by implementing the same training loop described in baseline.py: a factorization machine over the 5 categorical fields (user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, dur_bucket), embedding dim k=16, Adam lr=0.001, batch size 8192, pointwise BCE loss, early stopping on validation primary with patience 4. The expected result is ~0.6016 on validation primary. This establishes the working pipeline I'll build on in subsequent iterations.

I want to understand the data distribution and feature statistics to identify what signals are available for improving ranking. Specifically: label rates per user/feature, the within-user variance of features (since only features varying across a user's small candidate set matter), duration statistics, and the degree of popularity concentration among videos. This will determine whether there are exploitable signals beyond the FM baseline's 5-field approach.

Adding video_type and music_type as FM categorical features will improve ranking by giving the model content-level signals that vary within a user's impression list, allowing better discrimination between videos of different types for the same user
mechanism: In the FM, cross-feature interactions between (user_id × video_type) and (user_id × music_type) effectively learn per-user affinities for content categories. Since video_type and music_type vary across the ~5 videos a user sees in evaluation, these interaction terms will differ across the candidate list and contribute to reranking. The current model has video_id embeddings but those are highly sparse (7583 videos); video_type generalizes across videos the user may not have seen before.

evidence.task_structure: 81.8% of valid users see different video_ids; video_type/music_type cluster those video_ids into fewer categories, enabling better generalization. Within-user variation in content type is a direct requirement for the feature to contribute to ranking.
evidence.previous_experiments: Node 0 confirms the FM architecture works; the established findings say using all 13 static features showed no gain, but that used user-side features — item-side content features (video_type, music_type) are qualitatively different.

proposed_change: Load video_features_basic_pure.csv, extract video_type and music_type per video_id, join to all splits. Add 'video_type' and 'music_type' as two additional categorical fields in the FM feature vector (expanding FIELDS from 5 to 7).
expected_result: 0.001-0.004 improvement in validation primary (0.602-0.606); effect may be small since video_id already partially captures per-video content patterns, but category-level generalization should help for new/unseen video combinations
falsification_condition: If VAL_PRIMARY does not exceed 0.602 (no improvement beyond noise floor of 0.002 above 0.6018), the hypothesis is wrong — video_type/music_type do not add signal beyond what video_id already captures

risks.leakage: video_type and music_type are static item metadata, not time-varying statistics — no leakage risk
risks.overfitting: Adding 2 more fields adds ~few hundred embedding parameters; trivial relative to 1.14M training rows — negligible overfitting risk
risks.runtime: Minimal increase; 7 fields vs 5, same FM structure — runtime stays well under 5 minutes

candidates_considered: Add video_type + music_type from video_features_basic_pure.csv as FM categorical features — simple one-field addition, directly varies within-user
Compute per-user × video_type affinity score from training history — more complex but directly captures preference heterogeneity; continuous feature needs different FM handling
Switch from pointwise BCE to pairwise BPR loss — directly optimizes ranking, but major architectural change with uncertain gain given the already-reasonable performance
reflection: Node 0 reproduced the FM baseline at 0.6018 (matching reference 0.6016). Node 1 was EDA-only and produced no submission. The baseline is solid. The key insight from the established findings is that only features varying within a user's impression list matter for ranking. The EDA confirms duration varies heavily (std=72k ms), and 81.8% of users see different videos. The video_features_basic_pure.csv file contains video_type and music_type fields that provide content signal beyond video_id and vary across videos shown to the same user.
